cover.alt: Brindle and Leo under the big oak tree, with the mouse twins between them, one gray with dust and one with a leaf on her ear

text: Pip and Pebble were mouse twins. They lived in a hollow log by the stream.
They had the same round ears. They had the same pink tails. They had the same quick little paws.
And they did not agree on one thing. Not one.
Pip said the sky was blue. Pebble said it was more of a gray. They argued until lunch.

media.alt: Pip and Pebble, the mouse twins, stand nose to nose by their hollow log at the stream

text: The twins had one big problem. No one could tell them apart.
“Good morning, Pip!” sang Wren.
“I am Pebble,” said Pebble.
“Good morning, Pebble!” sang Wren to the other twin.
“I am Pip,” said Pip.
Wren flew off in a huff. Twins were too hard. News was more fun.

media.alt: Wren flies off in a huff while the twins stand side by side

text: Tansy did not know which was which. So she just called them both “Pip-Pebble.”
Moss did not know which was which. He just waved at the log.
“Hi, twins,” said Moss. “Hi to both of you. Or just one of you. Hi.”
Then he rolled into a ball, just to be safe.

media.alt: Tansy scratches her head at the twins while Moss peeks out of his ball

text: “It is not fair,” said Pip. “I am the older twin!”
“By one minute,” said Pebble. “And I am the smarter twin.”
“By zero minutes,” said Pip.
They argued about that until the moon came up. But no one in the Hollow was there to hear it.

media.alt: The twins argue by their log under the first stars of the evening

text: The best nap spot was under the big oak tree. It was soft. It was warm. The sun hit it all day.
Brindle the old dog had napped there for ten summers.
Leo the lion had napped there for two.
They liked to share it. Brindle slept on one side. Leo slept on the other side. They were old pals.

media.alt: Brindle and Leo nap side by side in the sunny spot under the big oak tree

text: Then one day, Leo rolled over in his sleep. His big, fluffy mane went FLOMP, onto Brindle.
Brindle woke up with a mouth full of fur.
“PTOO!” said Brindle.
“Sorry,” said Leo. “My mane has a mind of its own.”
“Then your mane can nap on the hill,” said Brindle. “An old dog needs his sleep.”

media.alt: Leo rolls over in his sleep and his big mane lands on Brindle with a FLOMP

text: So Brindle took his naps by the stream. Leo took his naps up on the hill.
They did not share. They did not talk. They did not even wave.
Brindle could not sleep. The stream was too wet.
Leo could not sleep. The hill was too windy.
Leo’s wish ball sat in the grass. It was dim and gray.

media.alt: Brindle naps alone by the wet stream while Leo sulks up on the windy hill

text: Pip was Brindle’s helper. At nap time, he kept Brindle’s green bandana safe in his log.
Pebble was Leo’s helper. Each day, she brushed the burrs out of his mane.
“Brindle misses Leo,” said Pip.
“Leo misses Brindle,” said Pebble.
For once, the twins agreed.

media.alt: Pip helps Brindle by the stream while Pebble helps Leo on the hill

text: “They just need to talk,” said Pip.
“But Brindle will not go up the hill,” said Pebble.
“And Leo will not go down to the stream,” said Pip.
The twins sat on their log. They had to think. They sat and sat.
Then Pebble’s ears went up. “No one can tell us apart,” she said. “So let’s swap!”

media.alt: The twins sit on their log and think hard

text: Here was the plan. Pip would go to Leo and act like Pebble. Pebble would go to Brindle and act like Pip.
Each twin had one job. “Come to the oak tree at dusk,” they would say. “There is a surprise.”
“And the surprise is each other!” said Pip.
It was the best plan they ever had. They did not even argue about it. Much.

media.alt: The twins make their plan by the log, with paw prints going two ways

text: There was just one snag. The twins did not look quite the same.
So Pip rolled in the dust by the path. He rolled and rolled. When he got up, he was as gray as a stone.
Pebble had a tiny notch in the top of one ear. So she put a leaf on her ear, like a hat. She held it on with string from her bag of scraps.
Now they looked the same. Well, almost.

media.alt: Pip rolls in a pile of dust and turns gray, and Pebble ties a leaf over her ear

text: Tansy ran by with a nut. She stopped.
“Hi, Pip-Pebble,” said Tansy. “Hi, other Pip-Pebble. Why is there a leaf on your ear?”
“It is a hat,” said Pebble.
“It is a nice hat,” said Tansy. Then she ran off to hide her nut.
Then she forgot where she hid it. Tansy was good at hiding nuts. Finding them, not so much.

media.alt: Tansy stops with a nut and stares at the leaf on Pebble’s ear

text: Pip went up the hill to Leo.
“Hello, Pebble,” said Leo. “Time to brush my mane!”
Pip had never brushed a mane. He did not know where to start. He went in on the left.
Leo’s mane was like a big gold bush. It was very dark in there. Pip got lost in the fluff.

media.alt: Dusty gray Pip gets lost in Leo’s big fluffy mane

text: “Pebble?” said Leo. “Are you in there?”
“Yes!” came a small squeak. Then, “Which way is out?”
At last, Pip popped out by Leo’s ear. He had grass on his back and a burr on his nose.
Leo gave him a long look. “You brush like a new mouse,” he said.
“Come to the oak at dusk,” said Pip fast. “There is a surprise!” And he ran.

media.alt: Pip pops out by Leo’s ear with a burr on his nose, and Leo gives him a long look

text: Pebble went down to the stream to see Brindle.
“Hello, Pip,” said Brindle. “Did you bring my bandana?”
Pebble did not know where Pip kept the bandana. She looked in a log. It was full of nuts. Not that log! She looked by the stream.
At last she found a striped sock by the barn. It was the giant’s sock. It would have to do!

media.alt: Pebble finds the giant’s striped sock by the barn while Brindle waits

text: Pebble set the sock on Brindle’s neck.
Brindle sniffed the sock. Then he sniffed Pebble. His old nose was still very, very good.
“Hmm,” he said slowly. “Pip, you smell like a leaf.”
“I… ate one,” said Pebble.
“Hmm,” said Brindle again. But he said he would come to the oak at dusk.

media.alt: Brindle sniffs Pebble, with the striped sock around his neck

text: At dusk, Brindle came to the oak tree. Leo came too.
They saw each other. They both stopped.
“Oh,” said Brindle.
“Oh,” said Leo.
The whole Hollow hid in the grass to watch. Moss hid the best. He was a ball.

media.alt: At dusk, Brindle and Leo face each other under the oak while Moss hides as a ball

text: Just then, a big gust of wind came down the hill. WHOOSH!
It blew the leaf off Pebble’s ear. There was the tiny notch.
It blew the dust off Pip’s back. Under the dust, his fur was warm and brown.
The twins did not look the same at all. Not one bit.

media.alt: A gust of wind blows the leaf off Pebble’s ear and the dust off Pip

text: Brindle looked at the twin by his paw. “You have a notch in your ear,” he said. “Pip has no notch. You are Pebble!”
Leo looked at the twin by his tail. “And you are brown,” he said. “With short whiskers. You must be Pip!”
The twins looked at each other. “Oops,” they said.
The trick was up.

media.alt: Brindle looks down at Pebble’s notched ear, and Leo looks at brown Pip

text: “We just wanted you to be friends again,” said Pebble.
“You both miss each other,” said Pip. “You are just too stubborn to say it.”
Brindle and Leo were still for a long time. Then Leo began to laugh.
“I DO miss you,” said Leo. “The hill is too windy.”
“The stream is too wet,” said Brindle. “And I miss your bad jokes.”
Leo’s wish ball began to glow blue.

media.alt: Leo laughs and his wish ball glows blue while the twins look on

text: From then on, the two old pals shared the nap spot again. Leo’s mane was not a problem now. It was a pillow.
And the Hollow learned the trick at last.
Pip is the brown twin, with short whiskers.
Pebble is the gray twin, with a notch in her ear.

media.alt: Brindle naps on Leo’s mane like a pillow, with Pip and Pebble in front

text: The next morning, Wren flew down with big news.
“News! News!” she sang. “Pip is brown! Pebble has a notch!”
Then she landed on the log. She looked at the twins.
“Good morning, Pebble!” she said to Pip.
Pip and Pebble looked at each other. And for once, they both laughed.

media.alt: Wren lands on the log and says good morning to the wrong twin
